business: yerby, a cold-brewed sparkling yerba mate drink in a 330 ml can, launching in Czechia
by_segment: Active health-focused adult (sport most weeks, eats clean)
why_not: I like that there are no sweeteners, but paying almost 690 CZK up front with delivery for twelve cans of something I've never tasted is a lot when a Red Bull Zero is 45 at the shop. I'd rather grab one can at a café with the voucher first, but I don't have the voucher without buying the pack.

54 crowns a can is almost double what I pay for Big Shock or Monster when the 4-packs are on offer, and I'm not committing 649 plus shipping to twelve cans of something I've never tasted. I'd grab a free tasting can at an event, but I won't pay for a whole pack.

I grab a Monster or Red Bull at the petrol station or Tesco on the way, no thinking involved. Pre-ordering a 12-pack for 649 plus 39 delivery to a pickup point is more effort than my energy habit is worth, and at 54 a can it costs more than what I already drink.

I grab a cold Monster at the petrol station or Albert on the way, I don't plan my energy drinks a week ahead. Committing 649 CZK to a 12-pack of something with less caffeine than my usual can, before I've even tasted it, isn't how I buy.

The label is actually good, no sweeteners and only fruit sugar, but I'm not ordering a 12-pack of a drink I've never tasted and then walking to a pickup point for it. If I passed one of those partner cafés I might try a can, but I'm not going to look for one.

I grab my can at the petrol station or a shop before a night shift or training, I'm not prepaying 649 for twelve cans and going to a pickup point. The partner cafés are closed when I'm awake and working, so there's no way for me to just try one.

I'm not paying 649 plus shipping for twelve cans of something I've never tasted and already suspect tastes like bitter grass tea. I'd grab a free tasting can at an event or a single one at a café first, and that's it for now.

I like the clean label and the 80 mg of caffeine, but I'm not paying almost 700 CZK for twelve cans of something that might taste like bitter grass tea. I get my pre-workout cans from GymBeam for a lot less, so I'd want to taste one before I commit to a whole pack.
why_yes: A numbered first-run Czech can is exactly the kind of thing I try and post, so I'd grab one single can at a partner cafe for 59 CZK. I'm not paying 649 for twelve of something that might taste like grass tea before I've had one.

The label is short and clean: water, yerba mate, fruit concentrate, no sweeteners or preservatives, 4 g sugar. That is rare in a can, and 54 CZK is nothing for me, so I'd buy one pack to see if it fits my pre-training slot instead of my homemade matcha.

I'd grab a single can from the café fridge after pilates or with lunch because 4 g of sugar and natural caffeine is exactly what I look for on a label. I won't order a 12-pack of something I've never tasted, though; if the first can isn't bitter I'll keep buying it at the café.
